title: Compare predictive methods on retained data
purpose: Produce a bounded baseline, inspect measured failures, and justify one follow-up.
instructions: Read the Study objective, reviewed plan, exact input revisions, prior findings, challenges and failed operations before proposing work.
Inspect annotations and source permissions. Declare training, development and evaluation roles. Never infer scientific meaning from filenames.
Record what the baseline can predict, including coverage and explicit behavior for unseen targets. Check null and emission behavior before interpreting effect predictions.
Use the declared split unit and complete evaluation panel. Pin method revisions, preprocessing, seeds and runtime generations.
Delegate only a distinct uncertainty with a deliverable, evidence basis and decision consequence. Reuse existing measurements; agreement between agents is not validation.
Run the baseline within the allowance. Read its actual diagnostic outputs. Propose one follow-up that addresses an observed limitation; retaining the baseline is a valid outcome.
Report metric values, coverage, failures, limitations and exact evidence references. Distinguish execution success, predictive quality and human acceptance.

For blinded evaluation, freeze all candidates before evaluation access. Ordinary folders and Project permissions do not isolate a shell-capable agent. Instructions cannot grant access or authorize installs.
limitations: Does not select a scientifically valid model automatically
Runtime and source licences require separate checks
Contains no executable code or execution authority
